text:
lina: FYI starting a staged rollout for v3.2.1 in ~2m (change window 22:00-23:00 UTC). DeployBot preflight green. Canary will be 5% in eu-west-1.

deploy-bot: Deploybot: preflight checks PASS. Canary group created (5%) and traffic routed.

raj: quick metric attach https://metrics.internal/redwood/canary/1730 p95 looks +15% vs baseline, taily.

tom: Any spike in errors or strictly latency?

sre-oncall: 5xx flat. We're seeing kvcache evictions jump on canary instances — eviction rate x3 at 22:01. Memory steady.

alan: Could be new attention caching behavior with longer sequences in this model build. Does v3.2.0-quant exhibit same churn?

lina: Not on previous canaries. I'm leaning to pause increase and pin canary to v3.2.0-quant while we triage. Thoughts?

raj: Vote: hold and pin. :thumbsup:

tom: Hold. need logs to confirm root cause.

alan: Hold from me. Also file an incident ticket for deeper trace.

lina: @deploy-bot can you pause further percent bumps and @tom/raj can one of you pin the canary to the quant variant?

deploy-bot: Deploybot: traffic increase suspended per request.

tom: On it. Pinning canary allocation in eu-west-1 to v3.2.0-quant now...

deploy-bot: Deploybot: canary pinned to v3.2.0-quant (allocation: canary-eu-west-1-7).

lina: Thanks. Watch p95 and eviction metrics for 10m, please. If stable we reconvene for a cautious bump to 10-20%.

sre-oncall: Snapshot in 5m shows eviction rate falling back to baseline after pin. Posting logs below for the spike:```
[22:01:03] kvcache: evict key=ctx-892 shard=2 reason=mem_pressure
[22:01:03] model: req=id=cb77 seq_len=4096 latency=512ms
[22:01:04] kvcache: miss key=ctx-892
```

raj: Adding release notes line: "Temporary pin of eu-west-1 canary to v3.2.0-quant due to observed KV cache eviction-induced latency on v3.2.1 canary." OK to commit?

lina: Fine by me. I'll update release notes and create an investigation ticket (INV-2026).

alan: One operational note 1: ensure rollback playbook updated with pin steps and who owns re-unpin.

lina: noted. We'll keep this thread open for the next 15m then close if stable. :slightly_smiling_face:
